methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Drones & Autonomous (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 6 same-sector peers exist in Drones & Autonomous, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Waymo is a private-stage autonomous vehicle company in the Drones & Autonomous sector, currently valued at $126B after raising $16B+. The sector peer universe consists of 6 private companies (Wayve, Zipline, Joby Aviation, Nuro, Archer Aviation, and one additional peer) with no public comparables available for direct benchmarking.

Peer-median valuation proved inapplicable due to insufficient narrow-stage datapoints. The Drones & Autonomous sector lacks three or more same-stage or adjacent-stage peers with similar valuation tier, which would be required for reliable median comparison. While six same-sector peers exist, filtering for stage, maturity, and valuation alignment yields fewer than the minimum three observations needed to establish a defensible multiple. An all-sector median approach was rejected as it would conflate fundamentally different business models and risk profiles within autonomous mobility.

The analysis does not support a triangulated valuation range at this time. The primary constraint is sparse comparability: Waymo's $126B valuation places it in a tier above most private-sector drones and autonomous peers, and the absence of public comps eliminates revenue/EBITDA multiple benchmarking. Resolution of valuation would require either (1) identification of additional same-tier private comparables with disclosed financials, (2) forward-looking DCF modeling with explicit assumptions on deployment timeline and unit economics, or (3) wait-and-see pricing from announced IPO or secondary transactions.
